sentences.text: To find geographic range, find the distance to the horizon from the light and from your eye, and add them.
The distance to the horizon in nautical miles is one point one seven times the square root of the height in feet.
For a light sixty-four feet high, the square root is eight, so its horizon is about nine point four miles.
For your eye at nine feet, the square root is three, so your horizon is about three and a half miles.
Add them, and the geographic range is about twelve point nine miles.
If the light’s luminous range tonight is fifteen miles, you’ll still only see it at about twelve point nine miles, because the lesser range wins.
